subject: Model evaluation follow-up — regression after v2.1.0
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acme.ai>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@acme.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-30T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Model evaluation follow-up — regression after v2.1.0

Hi Sara / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation and really helpful context on the summaries/claims use case. Per our call, I wanted to capture the next steps and recommended model/profile based on the evaluation we ran against your prompt set.

Recap of what we discussed:
- Primary goal: factual accuracy on product/financial summaries, minimize hallucinations; latency target <= 400ms p95 for interactive UI.
- Dataset: 2k production prompts + 200 edge cases you shared (attached).
- Observed regression: after your environment switched to upstream model v2.1.0 (released this week), a subset of prompts show increased hallucination rate vs. v2.0.x.

Recommendations / next steps:
1) Short-term: pin inference to model-v2.0.4 for the critical routes where accuracy is priority (we can do this immediately on Dedicated).
2) Engineering: we’ll run a diff on logits/attention that flagged the regression and share a CSV of failing prompts + model outputs (attached: acme-bench-diff-v2.0_vs_v2.1.csv).
3) Evaluation: use our suggested prompt set adjustments (attached: acme-prompt-set-recommendations.json) and run the rerank/QA checks; I recommend the strict QA filter for the top-3 responses for now.
4) Rollback plan: If the regression is confirmed, schedule a rollback window with minimal downtime; Dev, Marcus — can you confirm feasible rollback timing below?

I’ve cc’d Marcus (CS) and Dev (Infra) to own the rollback + diffs.

Would you be available for a 30-min sync today at 3pm PT to review the failing examples and agree on the rollback window? If that doesn’t work, we can do tomorrow morning.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: acme-bench-diff-v2.0_vs_v2.1.csv, acme-prompt-set-recommendations.json

From: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-07-30T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model evaluation follow-up — regression after v2.1.0

Marissa,

Thanks for the quick recap and for running the evals — really appreciate it. We started seeing the issue late last week after our infra team accepted the v2.1.0 rollout. In a handful of cases the model confidently invents product features that don't exist (see inline examples below).

Example 1 (prompt id: edge-142):
> "Give a short product summary for "Atlas Pro" and list supported export formats."

v2.0.4 result: "Atlas Pro supports CSV, JSON, and Parquet exports." (correct)
v2.1.0 result: "Atlas Pro supports CSV, JSON, Parquet, and native Excel .xlsx exports with model-indexed metadata." (hallucination)

Example 2 (prompt id: edge-177):
> "Does the product support scheduled exports?"

v2.0.4: "No scheduled exports today; recommended workaround is X."
v2.1.0: "Yes — scheduled exports are supported via the job-scheduler service." (incorrect)

This is customer impacting — a couple of enterprise customers have already observed inconsistencies. We’re open to doing the rollback; can you confirm what pin version you recommend and how long the rollback takes? Also please include suggested communications to customers so we can coordinate.

—Sara
Sara Jones
Head of Product
Acme AI
sara.jones@acme.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acme.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-30T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model evaluation follow-up — regression after v2.1.0

Thanks for the examples, Sara — very helpful. Quick update from infra/serving side:

- We pulled the failing prompts and re-ran locally with the v2.0.4 and v2.1.0 checkpoints; logs show consistent divergence in top-1 tokens starting ~step 18 for several prompts. We exported a diff CSV (attached in Marissa's original email).
- Short-term remediation: pin to v2.0.4 for the critical route. That’s a config change on Dedicated and will take <10 minutes to flip with no model warm-up required if we use a graceful route drain.
- Rollback window: we can do an immediate rollback at 14:00 PT today and monitor for 2 hours. If you prefer we can schedule 21:00 PT to minimize exposure for east-coast customers.
- Customer comms: recommend a short note: "We observed a model behavior change after a recent upgrade that impacts content accuracy on specific queries. We are reverting to the prior model version and will notify once monitoring confirms resolution; expected window: 14:00–16:00 PT." I can draft a one-paragraph comms and include affected prompt examples.

Longer-term: we’ll run a per-layer attention diff and metricized regression test (we’ll populate INF-2387 and share results). For now, pinning/v2.0.4 rollback is the safest path.

Action items:
- Marissa: confirm rollback timing with Acme (Sara/Tom).
- Marcus: prepare monitoring dashboard (latency, hallucination-rate per prompt set).
- Dev: draft comms and perform rollback; push to INF-2387 once diffs complete.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acme.ai>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@acme.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-30T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model evaluation follow-up — regression after v2.1.0

Sara / Tom — thanks for the quick replies. Tom, please let us know which window you prefer (14:00 PT or 21:00 PT). Our recommended default is 14:00 PT today to reduce the number of affected sessions, and we’ll monitor with Marcus for 2 hours post-rollback.

Mutual action plan (high-level):
- Today 14:00 PT: Dev to perform rollback to model-v2.0.4 on the production route. Marcus to monitor hallucination-rate by prompt set.
- Post-rollback (within 24h): Redwood to share diff CSV + INF-2387 ticket with attention logs and top-k token divergence.
- By EOD tomorrow: Acme to validate that the problematic prompts are resolved and share any residual examples.
- Next week: joint postmortem + plan for safe upgrade (canary + stricter QA gate).

If you approve, we’ll proceed with 14:00 PT and I’ll send the calendar invite + brief comms draft.

Thanks,
Marissa
(Quoted/Forwarded headers preserved in-line from prior messages)
